'''Isaiah Andre Canaan''' (pronounced Cannon; born May 21, 1991) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for [[Trabzonspor B.K.|Trabzonspor]] of the [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL). He was an [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] college player for the [[Murray State Racers men's basketball|Murray State Racers]].

==College career==
[[File:Isaiah Canaan 2011 Murray State University Men's Basketball.jpg|thumb|left|upright|Canaan at Murray State]]
Canaan, a 6'0" guard from [[Biloxi, Mississippi]], went to [[Murray State Racers men's basketball|Murray State]] after leading [[Biloxi High School]] to the 5A [[Mississippi]] state championship as a senior.<ref name=MSUBIO>{{cite web| title = MSU bio| publisher = Murray State Athletics| year = 2011 | url =http://goracers.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=2471&path=mbball| access-date = February 7, 2012}}</ref> Canaan had an instant impact for the Racers, as he averaged 10.4 [[points per game]] and led the Racers in three-point percentage at .485 as a freshman in the [[2009–10 Murray State Racers men's basketball team|2009–10 season]]. He was named 2010 [[Ohio Valley Conference]] (OVC) freshman of the year as the Racers went 17–1 in OVC play, winning the league. They also won the [[2010 Ohio Valley Conference men's basketball tournament|2010 OVC tournament]]. Canaan was named tournament MVP as he scored 16 points off the bench for the Racers in the final.<ref>{{cite web| title = Murray St. gets 30th win in earning NCAA berth| work = ESPN.com| year = 2010 | url =http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=300650093| archive-url =https://web.archive.org/web/20100320085154/http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=300650093| url-status =dead| archive-date =March 20, 2010| access-date = February 7, 2012}}</ref> Murray State went on to knock off 4-seeded [[2009–10 Vanderbilt Commodores men's basketball team|Vanderbilt]] in the [[2010 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|NCAA tournament]], before losing to eventual national runner-up [[2009–10 Butler Bulldogs men's basketball team|Butler]] 54–52 in the second round.

In his sophomore year, Canaan raised his scoring average to 11.7 points per game and was named to the first team All-OVC team. He led the Racers to their second straight OVC regular-season championship. Though they lost in the [[2011 Ohio Valley Conference men's basketball tournament|2011 OVC tournament]], the Racers again went to the postseason in the form of the [[2011 National Invitation Tournament]].

As a junior, Canaan and the Racers had a breakout season. Canaan was named to the preseason All-OVC team. Led by Canaan, Murray State began the season with a school and conference record 23 straight wins. Included was a [[2011 Great Alaska Shootout]] tournament championship, as Canaan was named MVP, scoring 36 in the tournament final.<ref>{{cite news |title= Murray State wins the Great Alaska Shootout |author= Jeremy Peters |newspaper= Anchorage Daily News |date= November 27, 2011 |url= http://www.adn.com/2011/11/26/2190476/murray-state-wins-great-alaska.html |access-date= February 7, 2012 |url-status= dead |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20120201183241/http://www.adn.com/2011/11/26/2190476/murray-state-wins-great-alaska.html |archive-date= February 1, 2012 }}</ref> Canaan, the Racers' leading scorer, was named to the finalist lists for the [[Bob Cousy Award]]<ref>{{cite web| title = 2012 Cousy Award Finalists| publisher = Cousy Award| year = 2012| url = http://www.cousyaward.com/finalists.php| access-date = February 7, 2012| url-status = dead| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20120218222555/http://www.cousyaward.com/finalists.php| archive-date = February 18, 2012}}</ref> and the [[Oscar Robertson Award]].<ref>{{cite web| title = USBWA Oscar Robertson midseason watch list| publisher = USBWA.com| year = 2012 | url =http://www.sportswriters.net/usbwa/news/2012/oscar120206.html| access-date = February 7, 2012}}</ref>

On February 17, 2018, Murray State retired Canaan's number 3 jersey.<ref>{{cite news| last = Wells | first = Adam | title = Canaan's #3 jersey retired by Murray State| publisher = wpsdlocal16.com| date = February 17, 2018 | url =http://www.wpsdlocal6.com/2018/02/17/canaans-3-jersey-retired-murray-state/| access-date = February 18, 2018}}</ref>

==Professional career==

===Houston Rockets (2013–2015)===
Canaan was selected 34th overall in the [[2013 NBA draft]] by the [[Houston Rockets]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-draft-isaiah-canaan Rockets Draft Isaiah Canaan]</ref> On July 15, 2013, he signed his rookie scale contract with the Rockets.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/rockets/news/roster-taking-shape-rockets Roster Taking Shape for the Rockets]</ref> During his rookie season, he had multiple assignments with the [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]] of the [[NBA Development League]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/dleague/assignments_2013_14.html 2013–14 NBA Assignments] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140703151241/http://www.nba.com/dleague/assignments_2013_14.html |date=2014-07-03 }}</ref>

On February 3, 2014, Canaan was named to the Prospects All-Star roster for the 2014 NBA D-League All-Star Game.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/nba_dleague_all_star_2014_02_03.html Eighth Annual NBA D-League All-Star Game Features 16 Players With NBA Experience] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140207181043/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/nba_dleague_all_star_2014_02_03.html |date=2014-02-07 }}</ref>

On November 26, 2014, Canaan scored a career high 24 points on 9-of-16 shooting in the 102–89 win over the Sacramento Kings.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20141126/SACHOU/gameinfo.html |title=Harden leads Rockets past Kings 102–89 |access-date=2014-11-27 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160609162959/http://www.nba.com/games/20141126/SACHOU/gameinfo.html |archive-date=2016-06-09 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Two days later, Cannan left the game against the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] with a left ankle sprain and didn't return. At the time he left the injury, he was the Rockets leading scorer with 13 points. As a result of the injury, he was required to wear a walking boot and use crutches. After being forced to sit out for a few weeks to heal, he was reassigned to the Rio Grande Valley Vipers on January 11, 2015, while he continued his recovery.<ref>[http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/?id=4914422 Rockets Assign Canaan to the NBA D-League's Rio Grande Valley Vipers]</ref> On January 26, 2015, he was recalled by the Rockets after averaging 21.0 points, 8.5 assists and 3.1 rebounds per game.<ref>[http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/?id=4920043 Rockets Recall Canaan from Rio Grande Valley Vipers]</ref>[[File:Isaiah Canaan Rockets.JPG|thumb|right|upright|Canaan with the Houston Rockets in 2014]]

===Philadelphia 76ers (2015–2016)===
On February 19, 2015, Canaan was traded, along with a 2015 second-round draft pick, to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] in exchange for [[K. J. McDaniels]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/150219-trades-release|title=Sixers Acquire Two First-round Picks, A 2015 Second-round Pick, Isaiah Canaan, And JaVale McGee|work=NBA.com|date=February 19, 2015|access-date=February 19, 2015}}</ref> Three days later, he made his debut for the 76ers as the team's starting point guard. In 29 minutes of action, he recorded 14 points, 4 rebounds and 3 assists in a 103–98 loss to the Orlando Magic.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20150222/PHIORL/gameinfo.html |title=Vucevic powers Magic past 76ers 103–98 |access-date=2015-02-23 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150311031658/http://www.nba.com/games/20150222/PHIORL/gameinfo.html |archive-date=2015-03-11 |url-status=dead }}</ref> On March 4, 2015, he recorded career highs of 31 points and eight three-pointers in a 123–118 overtime loss to the Oklahoma City Thunder.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20150304/PHIOKC/gameinfo.html |title=Westbrook has career-high 49, lifts Thunder past 76ers in OT |access-date=2015-03-05 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151122061711/http://www.nba.com/games/20150304/PHIOKC/gameinfo.html |archive-date=2015-11-22 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

On March 21, 2016, Canaan made three three-pointers against the [[Indiana Pacers]], giving him 158 for the 2015–16 season and breaking a tie with [[Allen Iverson]] for No. 5 on the franchise's single-season list.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160321/PHIIND/gameinfo.html |title=Pacers' playoff push gets jumpstart with win over 76ers |access-date=2016-03-22 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160324101650/http://www.nba.com/games/20160321/PHIIND/gameinfo.html |archive-date=2016-03-24 |url-status=dead }}</ref> On April 8, 2016, he was ruled out for the rest of the season with a torn labrum in his left shoulder.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.csnphilly.com/basketball-philadelphia-76ers/sixers-injury-update-isaiah-canaan-out-season-torn-labrum |title=Sixers Injury Update: Isaiah Canaan out for season with torn labrum |access-date=2016-04-09 |archive-date=2016-04-28 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160428072918/http://www.csnphilly.com/basketball-philadelphia-76ers/sixers-injury-update-isaiah-canaan-out-season-torn-labrum |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Chicago Bulls (2016–2017)===
On July 20, 2016, Canaan signed with the [[Chicago Bulls]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/bulls/news/release/bulls-sign-isaiah-canaan|title=BULLS SIGN ISAIAH CANAAN|work=NBA.com|date=July 20, 2016|access-date=July 20, 2016}}</ref> In [[2016–17 Chicago Bulls season|2016–17]], Canaan appeared in 39 games and averaged 4.6 points, 1.3 rebounds, 0.9 assists, and 0.56 steals in 15.2 minutes per game. He shot .364 from the field, .266 from three-point range and .909 from the free throw line. Canaan made his first career postseason appearance on April 23, 2017, against the [[Boston Celtics]] and logged his first career playoff start on April 26.<ref name=bulls-waive>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-waive-rajon-rondo-and-isaiah-canaan|title=BULLS WAIVE RAJON RONDO AND ISAIAH CANAAN|work=NBA.com|date=June 30, 2017|access-date=June 30, 2017}}</ref> On June 30, 2017, he was waived by the Bulls.<ref name="bulls-waive" />

===Return to Houston (2017)===
On September 24, 2017, Canaan signed with the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Thunder Adds Alford, Brown, Canaan and Thomas to Training Camp Roster|url=http://www.nba.com/thunder/news/alford-brown-canaan-thomas-170925|website=NBA.com|date=September 24, 2017|access-date=September 26, 2017}}</ref> He was waived by the Thunder on October 14 after appearing in three preseason games.<ref>{{cite web|title=Thunder Waives Four|url=http://www.nba.com/thunder/news/waives-four-171014|website=NBA.com|access-date=October 14, 2017|date=October 14, 2017}}</ref> On October 24, 2017, Canaan signed with the [[Houston Rockets]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Rockets sign guard Isaiah Canaan|url=http://www.chron.com/sports/rockets/article/Rockets-sign-guard-Isaiah-Canaan-12302453.php|website=chron.com|date=October 24, 2017|access-date=October 26, 2017}}</ref> He was waived by the Rockets four days later after appearing in one game.<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/usa/nba/251810/rockets-waive-isaiah-canaan.html Rockets waive Isaiah Canaan]</ref>

===Phoenix Suns (2017–2018)===
On December 12, 2017, Canaan was acquired by the [[Northern Arizona Suns]] of the [[NBA G League]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://northernarizona.gleague.nba.com/news/naz-suns-trade-nba-veteran-isaiah-canaan/ |title=NAZ Suns Trade for NBA Veteran Isaiah Canaan |access-date=2017-12-14 |archive-date=2020-09-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200920021531/https://northernarizona.gleague.nba.com/news/naz-suns-trade-nba-veteran-isaiah-canaan/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> The next day, he was called up by the [[Phoenix Suns]], after Phoenix received an injury hardship exemption.<ref>{{cite news|title=Phoenix Suns Sign Isaiah Canaan|url=http://www.nba.com/suns/press-release/phoenix-suns-sign-isaiah-canaan|access-date=December 14, 2017|work=NBA.com|date=December 13, 2017}}</ref> He made his debut with Phoenix on December 16, scoring 15 points and making three game-winning free throws with six seconds left in a 108–106 win over the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975185|title=Canaan helps Suns rally to beat T-Wolves 108–106|work=ESPN.com|date=December 16, 2017|access-date=November 29, 2018}}</ref> Two days later, he scored 17 points in a 97–91 win over the [[Dallas Mavericks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975199|title=Len, Suns complete 97–91 comeback win against Mavericks|work=ESPN.com|date=December 18, 2017|access-date=November 29, 2018}}</ref> With seven assists against Minnesota and six against Dallas,<ref>[https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/c/canaais01/gamelog/2018/ Isaiah Canaan 2017–18 Game Log]</ref> Canaan became the first player in Suns history to come off the bench and have at least 15 points and five assists in their first two games with the team.<ref>[https://twitter.com/sbordow/status/943248628038090752 Amazing stat: Canaan first player in Suns...]</ref> On December 23, 2017, the Suns retained him for the rest of the season.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/nba/suns/2017/12/23/phoenix-suns-isaiah-canaan-mike-james/979510001/|title=Canaan signs with Suns|date=December 23, 2017|work=AZCentral.com}}</ref> On January 31, 2018, Canaan fractured his left ankle while driving to the rim in the first quarter of their game against the Mavericks.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.nba.com/article/2018/01/31/phoenix-suns-guard-isaiah-canaan-suffers-gruesome-ankle-injury#/|title=Phoenix Suns guard Isaiah Canaan suffers gruesome ankle injury while driving to rim|date=January 31, 2018|work=NBA.com|access-date=January 31, 2018}}</ref> He was subsequently waived by the Suns on February 8.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/suns/press-release/official-phoenix-suns-waive-isaiah-canaan Phoenix Suns Waive Isaiah Canaan]</ref>

On August 3, 2018, Canaan re-signed with the Phoenix Suns.<ref>[https://www.nba.com/suns/press-release/phoenix-suns-re-sign-isaiah-canaan Phoenix Suns Re-Sign Isaiah Canaan]</ref> In the Suns' season opener on October 17, 2018, Canaan got the start at point guard and had eight points, six rebounds and seven assists in a 121–100 win over the [[Dallas Mavericks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore?gameId=401070216|title=Mavericks vs. Suns – Box Score|work=ESPN.com|date=October 17, 2018|access-date=October 17, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401070216|title=Booker's late onslaught lifts Suns past Mavs 121–100|work=ESPN.com|date=October 17, 2018|access-date=October 17, 2018|quote=Isaiah Canaan, coming back from a gruesome leg injury sustained on the same court last season, got the start at point guard.}}</ref> On November 14, he had 19 points and made all five of his 3-pointers in a 116–96 win over the [[San Antonio Spurs]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401070892|title=T.J. Warren scores 27 points, Suns beat Spurs 116–96|work=ESPN.com|date=November 14, 2018|access-date=November 14, 2018}}</ref> Canaan began the season as the team's starting point guard before coach [[Igor Kokoškov]] moved [[Devin Booker]] to the point and inserted rookie [[Mikal Bridges]] into the starting lineup.<ref name=suns-clippers>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401070996|title=Clippers extend home winning streak to 9 by beating Suns|work=ESPN.com|date=November 28, 2018|access-date=November 29, 2018}}</ref> On November 28, he was waived by the Suns.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/suns/suns-waive-isaiah-canaan|title=Suns Waive Isaiah Canaan|work=NBA.com|date=November 28, 2018|access-date=November 28, 2018}}</ref> Kokoškov noted that it "was a business decision" to waive Canaan.<ref name="suns-clippers" />

===Minnesota Timberwolves (2019)===
On January 30, 2019, Canaan signed a 10-day contract with the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/timberwolves-sign-guard-isaiah-canaan-10-day-contract|title=Timberwolves Sign Guard Isaiah Canaan to 10-Day Contract|date=January 30, 2019|work=NBA.com|access-date=January 30, 2019}}</ref> On February 11, he signed a second 10-day contract with the Timberwolves.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/timberwolves-sign-guard-isaiah-canaan-second-10-day-contract|title=Timberwolves Sign Guard Isaiah Canaan to Second 10-Day Contract|work=NBA.com|date=February 11, 2019|access-date=February 12, 2019}}</ref> Following the expiration of his second 10-day contract, the Timberwolves decided not to sign Canaan for the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite web|last=Suleymanov|first=Mark|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2019/02/timberwolves-will-not-sign-isaiah-canaan-for-rest-of-season.html|title=Timberwolves Will Not Sign Isaiah Canaan For Rest Of Season|work=hoopsrumors.com|date=February 23, 2019|access-date=February 25, 2019}}</ref>

===Milwaukee Bucks (2019)===
On February 25, 2019, Canaan signed a 10-day contract with the [[Milwaukee Bucks]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/release/milwaukee-bucks-sign-isaiah-canaan-10-day-contract|title=Milwaukee Bucks Sign Isaiah Canaan to 10-Day Contract|work=NBA.com|date=February 25, 2019|access-date=February 25, 2019}}</ref> but was released on March 3.<ref>{{cite tweet|number=1102334638956179456|user=Bucks|title=The Bucks have released guard Isaiah Canaan from his 10-day contract. Originally signed to a 10-day contract on F…<!-- full text of tweet that Twitter returned to the bot (excluding links) added by TweetCiteBot. This may be better truncated or may need expanding (TW limits responses to 140 characters) or case changes. --> |accessdate=March 3, 2019|date=March 3, 2019}}</ref>

=== Stockton Kings (2019–2020) ===
On August 22, 2019, Canaan signed with [[Shandong Golden Stars]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association|CBA]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/isaiah-canaan-signs-with-shandong/|title=Isaiah Canaan signs with Shandong|date=August 22, 2019|newspaper=Sportando|language=En|access-date=August 22, 2019|archive-date=August 11, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200811032226/https://sportando.basketball/en/isaiah-canaan-signs-with-shandong/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On December 7, 2019, the [[Stockton Kings]] had acquired the returning right of Canaan with a third-round draft pick in the [[2020 NBA G League draft]] from the [[Austin Spurs]] for the returning rights of [[Cameron Reynolds]] and a second-round draft pick in the 2020 NBA G League Draft.<ref>{{cite tweet|number=1203373610619944960|user=StocktonKings|title=🚨 MOVES ALERT 🚨 Austin Spurs  will receive the returning player rights to Cam Reynolds and Stockton’s 2020 2nd rou…<!-- full text of tweet that Twitter returned to the bot (excluding links) added by TweetCiteBot. This may be better truncated or may need expanding (TW limits responses to 140 characters) or case changes. --> |accessdate=December 7, 2019|date=December 7, 2019}}</ref> Canaan made his Stockton debut on December 13, 2019. On January 19, 2020, Canaan scored 32 points and had six assists in a loss to the [[Agua Caliente Clippers]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Isaiah Canaan: Tallies 32 points Sunday |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/isaiah-canaan-tallies-32-points-sunday/ |access-date=February 8, 2020 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=January 20, 2020}}</ref>

===UNICS Kazan (2020–2022)===
On July 19, 2020, Canaan signed with [[BC UNICS|UNICS Kazan]] of the [[VTB United League]] and the [[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]].<ref>{{cite news|title= UNICS tabs scoring guard Canaan |url= https://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/aqns8q6bs9xxdw9w |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20200719212644/https://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/aqns8q6bs9xxdw9w |url-status= dead |archive-date= July 19, 2020 |date=July 19, 2020|website=[[EuroCup Basketball]]|access-date=July 19, 2020}}</ref> He averaged 14.2 points and 2.7 assists per game. Canaan re-signed with the team on July 7, 2021.<ref>{{cite web |title=Unics Kazan keeps Isaiah Canaan |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/unics-kazan-keeps-isaiah-canaan/ |website=Sportando |access-date=July 8, 2021 |date=July 7, 2021}}</ref> He left the team in early 2022 due to the [[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]].<ref name="auto1">{{Cite web |date=March 4, 2022 |title=Unics Kazan reportedly suing Jarrell Brantley for $250,000 |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/1316372/unics-kazan-reportedly-suing-jarrel-brantley-for-250000/ |website=Eurohoops}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://newswep.com/more-than-50-people-which-of-the-foreigners-left-the-russian-sports-clubs-football-rbc-sport/|title=More than 50 people. Which of the foreigners left the Russian sports clubs: RBC Sport|date=March 5, 2022|access-date=March 5, 2022|archive-date=March 5, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220305224516/https://newswep.com/more-than-50-people-which-of-the-foreigners-left-the-russian-sports-clubs-football-rbc-sport/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Galatasaray (2022)===
On March 31, 2022, he signed with [[Galatasaray S.K. (men's basketball)|Galatasaray Nef]] of the [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.galatasaray.org/haber/basketbol/erkek-basketbol/isaiah-canaan-galatasaray-nefte/50748|title=Isaiah Canaan Galatasaray Nef'te!|last=|first=|date=March 31, 2022|website=|publisher=Galatasaray|language=tr|access-date=March 31, 2022}}</ref> During his 12 appearances in Turkish BSL he averaged 11.3 points, 2.2 assists, 1.9 rebounds, and 0.6 steals per game.

===Olympiacos (2022–2024)===
On 8 July 2022, Canaan signed a two-year (1+1) deal with [[Olympiacos B.C.|Olympiacos]] of the [[Greek Basket League]] and the [[EuroLeague]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/isaiah-canaan-officially-signs-with-olympiacos/|title=Isaiah Canaan officially signs with Olympiacos|last=|first=|date=July 8, 2022|website=|publisher=Sportando|language=En|access-date=July 8, 2022}}</ref> On 5 July 2023, Olympiacos picked up the option in their mutual contract and Canaan remained with the club.

===KK Crvena Zvezda	(2024–2026)===
On September 29, 2025, Canaan suffered an injury to the [[anterior cruciate ligament|ACL]] during the first half of the VTB Supercup game against Dubai.<ref>{{cite web |title=Isaiah Canaan suffers ACL injury just before the start of the season |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/1872998/isaiah-canaan-suffers-acl-injury/ |website=Eurohoops |access-date=30 September 2025 |language=en |date=26 September 2025}}</ref>

===Trabzonspor (2026–present)===
On August 21, 2026, he signed with [[Trabzonspor B.K.|Trabzonspor]] of the [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL).<ref>{{Cite tweet |user=TSBasketResmi |number=2090807093716508733 |title=Hoş geldin, Isaiah Canaan}}</ref>
